packet.evaluation_question: Explain baseline investigations and how subsequent inflammatory-marker readings should be used.

evidence.text: Measure baseline C-reactive protein concentration when starting antibiotic treatment in babies who may have neonatal infection. Use this together with any subsequent readings to assess the likelihood of infection and response to treatment. [2021]
Get specialist radiological advice on investigations for a cerebrospinal fluid leak. [2024]
Provide emotional and pastoral support for family members and carers during hospitalisation. [2024]
Community child development services should follow up and assess the risk of long-term neurodevelopmental complications for at least 2 years after discharge. [2024]

claims.text: Obtain a baseline C‑reactive protein (CRP) measurement at the time antibiotics are started in any neonate being evaluated for early‑onset sepsis.

Interpret serial CRP results together with the initial value to gauge the probability of infection and to monitor response to therapy; falling values suggest a favorable response, whereas persistently high or rising values may indicate ongoing infection.
